title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 228
paragraphs: The men were buried where they fell; and for them, along with those who were killed before being dismissed by Leonidas, there is an inscription that reads:
“Here once, facing three hundred myriads of foes in battle, four thousand men from the Peloponnese made their stand.”
This is the inscription for the whole body; and for the Spartans alone there is this:
“Stranger, carry this word, we ask, to the Spartans — that lying here in this spot we remain, faithfully keeping their laws.”
This, then, for the Lacedaemonians; and for the soothsayer, as follows:

“This is the tomb of famed Megistias, whom the Median enemies slew where the Spercheios flows as they forded the stream — soothsayer who then, knowing clearly the fates that were coming, could not bring himself to abandon Sparta's good leaders in the fight.”

It was the Amphictyons who honored them with these inscriptions and memorial pillars, except in the case of the inscription to the soothsayer: that one, for the soothsayer Megistias, was composed by Simonides son of Leoprepes on account of guest-friendship.
